annotationRationale: The main method uses circle equations to derive the intersection line and read its slope. Tangent-radius geometry locates the centers. The alternative uses perpendicular bisectors and slope perpendicularity, with those concepts mapped only to that route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The centers are (4,0) and (0,10). Their circles meet at the origin and at (200/29,80/29), giving slope 2/5, choice E. The statement, choices, and key are consistent; no figure contradiction occurs.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The two useful accessible routes are retained: LIVE and AoPS Solution 2 through equation subtraction, and AoPS Solution 1 through the perpendicular common chord. The supplied polar-coordinate version gives the same relation with extra prerequisites and need not be added. No shared-bank methods are supplied.
review.annotationCheck: The revised assessed nodes cnm_h176 and cnm_h171 match the main equation method more precisely than the previous angle-based slope node. Tangent-radius perpendicularity is correctly supporting. The perpendicular-bisector and slope criteria are appropriately attached to the alternative route.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Tangency and the positive-axis conditions give the stated centers. Expanding the circle equations correctly produces x²+y²=8x and x²+y²=20y. Both intersections therefore satisfy 8x=20y, whose line has slope 2/5.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed LIVE and AoPS Solution 2 basis matches the supplied arguments. The explanation adds its own motivation and tangent-radius setup, uses original explanatory prose, and correctly identifies the references as third-party sources through source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first sentence explains why elimination is useful. Locating the centers, forming the equations, canceling terms, and identifying the line's slope are all visible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h176 covers writing the circles, cnm_h171 covers obtaining the slope from the resulting linear equation, and cnm_262 covers locating the centers. The cancellation is fully shown and does not require an unexplained radical-axis theorem.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All three exact native-topic links fit the steps used. Their use does not imply coverage of every criterion or broader national placement.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-C.A.2 supports the tangent-radius step. The supplied G-GPE.A.1, G-GPE.B.4, and A-REI.D.10 links for cnm_h176 are partial: the method uses circle equations and solution sets without deriving the circle formula or completing the square. cnm_h171 has no supplied US link, which is an honest alignment gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct nodes are precise and sufficient. The main route appropriately replaces the previous broad slope-concept assessment.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Both centers are equidistant from O and P, so their distinct connecting line is the perpendicular bisector of OP. Its slope is -5/2, making the slope of OP 2/5. Neither line creates an exceptional vertical-horizontal slope case.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately credits AoPS Solution 1. The perpendicular-bisector justification expands the source's stated common-chord fact in independent prose, with source-informed-original correctly used.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains the geometric idea, and the equal-radius equations establish the needed perpendicularity rather than merely asserting a circle theorem. The slope computation is complete.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_133, cnm_h167, cnm_h168, and cnm_262 directly cover the perpendicular-bisector criterion, two-point slope, perpendicular slopes, and tangent-radius setup.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact links for cnm_133, cnm_h167, and cnm_262 fit. The supplied partial cnm_h168 link is appropriate given its corrected scope; only its valid finite-slope perpendicularity criterion is used here.

G-GPE.B.4 and 8.EE.B.5/B.6 provide limited coordinate/slope overlap, without the proportional-model comparisons or similarity-based slope derivations required by those standards.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Every direct node is exercised, and the explanation supplies the common-chord consequence from the mapped perpendicular-bisector criterion.
